comments.text:
Bottom line, I believe the main problem is overpopulation. When families have too many children, more houses need to be built to accommodate the growing population. More children may end up spending time on the streets, families have to buy more food and other necessities, and this can also lead to more waste and garbage.

When a father struggles to provide for a large family, he may sometimes be pushed into criminal activities just to make ends meet. The mother may have to work multiple jobs, leaving the children without proper supervision. In some communities, particularly informal settlements, these problems can become more serious.

There should be regular saturation drives and enforcement operations in informal-settlement areas in Tondo, under bridges, in Parañaque, and throughout Metro Manila. Authorities should monitor illegal dumping, apprehend people involved in drug-related crimes, and address theft, snatching, and other violent crimes.

It is also much more difficult for a family to provide adequately for three or more children. To be honest, Metro Manila already feels too small and overcrowded for families with five or more members.

If the Philippines were to consider a **one-child policy**, perhaps within 10 years we could gradually begin to see a decline in population growth and some positive effects on housing, transportation, employment, food supply, and waste management.

I also believe the government should have a serious discussion about the **death penalty for the most serious crimes**, although this should be considered separately from population control because capital punishment should be based on justice and public safety, not on reducing the population.
